To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gene expression in mouse lungs exposed for 13-weeks to a tumorigenic concentration of V2O 5 was enriched in cAMP and PKA pathway signaling, hyaluronan metabolism, and sphingolypid metabolism.

V2O5 exposure to mouse lungs results in gene expression changes in hyaluronan, sphingolipids, adenylate-cyclase functions, cAMP signaling, and PKA activation, but not DNA-damage, cell cycle, and apoptosis pathways, suggesting a non-genotoxic mechanism of carcinogenicity.

V2O5 exposure in mouse lung results in gene expression changes in pathways related to lipid/lipoprotein metabolism, hyaluronan metabolism, sphingolipids, adenylate and c-AMP signaling, and PKA activation, which is distinct from gene expression changes seen in other mouse lung carcinogens.
